about.title: From game localization to AI engineering
about.description:
In 2026, I brought my two careers together: I designed and built, with Claude Code, a Python harness of LLM agents for the kind of work I know: game localization. A translator agent and parallel reviewers propose changes, hooks decide where each agent may write, a fixed rule merges the suggestions, and I decide what stays.

The engineering side matters as much as the AI side. I am in the back-end block at Infnet, learning Java with Spring Boot and JPA and starting a Java back-end project of my own. I also evaluate model outputs against rubrics (RLHF) on short-term projects.

I want to build AI systems that work in production: measured, tested, and with a person at the right point in the loop.

blog.post.1.title: Building Starr Corp: Office Mayhem - Behind the Scenes
blog.post.1.excerpt: An in-depth look at how I designed the logical engine and scene manager for my Brawl Stars tribute project.
blog.post.1.intro: Developing a Strategy Web Game in React and TypeScript
blog.post.1.p1: Creating Starr Corp: Office Mayhem was a great exercise in designing modular game logic within React's render loop. The core goal was to separate simulation rules from components, achieving clean, predictable updates.
blog.post.1.p2: In this article, I discuss the architecture behind the scene manager and custom engine hooks, showing how they manage brawler stats, choices, and office chaos levels without unnecessary re-renders.

project.title.7: agent-harness: guardrails for LLM agents, in code
project.description.7: A multi-agent harness for translation work, shown on an invented demo game. Python hooks decide, from a declarative map, where each agent may write; decisions an agent makes on its own go to a human approval queue; every write is logged for audit, and token cost is measured per agent. Works with Claude Code and Antigravity.
project.title.7.bullet1: One PreToolUse hook for both Claude Code and Antigravity, driven by a write-zone map (free, append-only, ask, blocked).
project.title.7.bullet2: A translator and parallel reviewers merged by a fixed rule in code, not an LLM judge: the human only sees what needs a decision.
project.title.7.bullet3: Standard-library Python, automated tests, and CI on Linux and Windows (Python 3.11 to 3.13).
project.title.8: rag-gta: local RAG with an evaluation set
project.description.8: Fully local RAG (Ollama, Chroma, and LangChain) over two corpora: Grand Theft Auto lore, with the source of every answer, and an EN → PT-BR localization glossary I co-authored. It has three retrieval modes and an evaluation set that scores retrieval, answers, and refusals separately. Built with Stephanie Pinho.
project.title.8.bullet1: Three retrieval modes (similarity, MMR, and multi-query) and question rewriting from the chat history.
project.title.8.bullet2: Evaluation with separate metrics (retrieval hit, answer hit, false refusal, correct refusal), run on GitHub Actions.
